original_question: If a numerical semigroup S satisfies Wilf's conjecture, determine whether its half S/2 = {x in N | 2x in S} must also satisfy Wilf's conjecture.
target_in_paper: Section 3, unnumbered open question after the discussion of symmetric and pseudo-symmetric numerical semigroups: "If a numerical semigroup verifies Wilf’s conjecture, then does so its half?"
correct_elements: The draft already matches the paper’s exact target very closely: it asks about preservation of Wilf’s conjecture under taking the half of a numerical semigroup, and it uses the correct quotient-by-2 definition S/2 = {x in N | 2x in S}. The direction of implication is the same as in the paper.
missing_details: The paper’s ambient convention is N = {0,1,2,...}; this should be stated because some authors use N for the positive integers.
The paper defines a numerical semigroup as a subset of N that is closed under addition, contains 0, and has finite complement; this is implicit in the draft.
The phrase "satisfies Wilf’s conjecture" should be unpacked using the paper’s exact inequality e(S)g(S) ≤ (e(S)-1)(F(S)+1).
The invariants in Wilf’s inequality should be defined explicitly: e(S) is the embedding dimension, g(S)=|N\S| is the genus, and F(S)=max(N\S) is the Frobenius number.
The universal quantifier should be made explicit: the paper asks this for every numerical semigroup S, with no additional assumptions such as symmetry, irreducibility, or bounded embedding dimension.
To make the question fully stand-alone, the conclusion should spell out that the same Wilf inequality is to be checked for S/2 itself, not only refer to it informally.
refined_question: Let S ⊆ N be a numerical semigroup, where N denotes the nonnegative integers, and define its half by S/2 = {x ∈ N : 2x ∈ S}. If S satisfies Wilf’s conjecture in the form e(S)g(S) ≤ (e(S)-1)(F(S)+1), where e(T) is the embedding dimension of a numerical semigroup T, g(T)=|N\T| is its genus, and F(T)=max(N\T) is its Frobenius number, must S/2 also satisfy Wilf’s conjecture, i.e. e(S/2)g(S/2) ≤ (e(S/2)-1)(F(S/2)+1)?
justification: The draft is targeting exactly the unnumbered open question posed in Section 3, page 19. That section first defines the quotient S/d = {x ∈ N : dx ∈ S} and explicitly names S/2 the "half" of S (Section 3, page 18). Earlier, Section 1 fixes the ambient definition of numerical semigroup and the invariants used throughout the paper: the Frobenius number F(S), the genus g(S)=|N\S|, and the embedding dimension e(S) (Section 1, pages 15-16). Wilf’s conjecture is stated there in the form e(S)g(S) ≤ (e(S)-1)(F(S)+1) (Section 1, page 16). In the immediate local context, the paper notes that symmetric numerical semigroups satisfy g(S)=(F(S)+1)/2, hence satisfy Wilf’s conjecture, and then asks whether Wilf’s conjecture descends to the half (Section 3, page 19). So the sharp paper-faithful rewrite is the same implication, with the notation and invariants made explicit.
